Instrument (EN): German Loneliness and Aloneness Scale for Children and Adolescents–Revised — new eight-item short form
Scales / measured domains (EN): Peer-related loneliness; Parent-related loneliness; two correlated subscales (not a universal global loneliness diagnosis)
Research provenance: Hessels S & Buecker S, Die Psychotherapie, published 2026-10-06, DOI 10.1007/s00278-026-00880-y; new shorter German LACA-R derived from 24-item parent. Secondary independent datasets N737 and N88, CFA and validity/reliability study. Evidence is preliminary for 10–15-year-olds.
DB locales: Not a published app.assessment_versions definition; live DB audit 149 keys /234 locale rows, 2026-10-24.
EN form: Article has English abstract, NOT psychometrically validated English respondent LACA-R-8 translation.
RU form: No independently validated Russian LACA-R-8 adaptation from this paper.
ES form: No independently validated Spanish LACA-R-8 adaptation from this paper.
Other translations: DE-DE German respondent shortened 8-item form psychometrically studied in two German secondary cohorts N737 and N88; short EDITION of LACA-R-24, not a separate loneliness construct.
Target population: Children and adolescents aged 10–15 years in German secondary cohorts, N737 and N88; school-age, non-diagnostic screening.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: OA journal/preprint availability and OSF dataset do not by themselves clear rehosting 8 original/derivative items, commercial e-administration, score/interpretation rights, translations, or guardian-consent requirements. Obtain creator and original LACA-R rights confirmation.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / PERMISSION_REQUIRED / MINOR-SAFETY-GATE. Two related dimensions, 8 items; 24-item LACA-R norms cannot simply be transferred. Preliminary factorial evidence, two secondary samples, German respondents only. Do not publicly administer before rights, child privacy, guardian consent/assent and safeguarding review.

Instrument (EN): Childhood Adversity Scale — original Turkish 59-item trauma-experience form
Scales / measured domains (EN): Early adverse experiences, cumulative childhood adversity (single factor); includes age/context/direct exposure/subjective impact as contextual metadata, not validated independent factor scores
Research provenance: Yanik M, Uysal B, Eruyar S et al., Frontiers in Psychiatry, published 2026-05-12, DOI 10.3389/fpsyt.2026.1701294. Construct development informed by retrospective review of 300 clinical DID case files (NOT 300 psychometric participants). 3 separate psychometric cohorts: EFA N338, CFA N413, convergent ACE N125. Final 59 items / one factor.
DB locales: Not registered or activated in app.assessment_versions; research-only metadata.
EN form: Authors explicitly note English translated adverse-event list lacks guideline-compliant translation/back-translation; NOT an EN validated respondent edition.
RU form: No independent RU-RU translation or validation established in this paper.
ES form: No independent ES respondent form validated in this paper.
Other translations: TR-TR original Turkish questionnaire developed and psychometrically studied (N338/N413/N125); English article translation NOT validated EN questionnaire.
Target population: Turkish adult respondents retrospectively reporting childhood adversities; measure informed by 300 dissociative-identity-disorder client files; convenience samples; not validated for schoolchildren or cross-cultural diagnosis.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: CC BY article does not settle separate item rights, online commercial administration, translations and scoring. Require author permission or documented applicable questionnaire item licence, original final Turkish form and clinical safeguarding prior to use.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / CLINICIAN_ONLY. Trauma-related sensitive exposure questions (child abuse); clinician-supervised consent, distress/crisis support and privacy mandatory. 59-item one-factor Turkish original, not ACE-IQ substitute. Some low factor loadings and CFA modifications limit generalization; English list is UNVALIDATED.

Instrument (EN): International Trauma Questionnaire — Child and Adolescent Version, Italian psychometric adaptation
Question count: 21 total: 12 PTSD/DSO symptom items + functional impairment items (functional impairment not analyzed in study)
Scales / measured domains (EN): PTSD: re-experiencing, avoidance, current threat (2 items each); DSO: affect dysregulation, negative self-concept, relationship disturbances (2 each). Two higher-order PTSD/DSO factors; impairment required for diagnosis but excluded.
Research provenance: Goffredo M et al., Journal of Traumatic Stress, first published 2026-09-03, DOI 10.1002/jts.70125. Italian translation/back-translation of original ITQ-CA, N488 Italian youth (432 community + 56 residential high-risk), ages 8–17; CFA on 12 symptom items only; second-order correlated PTSD/DSO CFI .990 TLI .986 RMSEA .045; approximate/partial invariance; no functional-impairment psychometric validation in this cohort.
DB locales: No Italian ITQ-CA published locale in app.assessment_versions; adult ITQ registered is same broad family but different age/version; research-only.
EN form: English ITQ-CA original available; this study is NOT an independent new EN respondent-language validation.
RU form: No independently validated RU respondent ITQ-CA translation from this Italian study.
ES form: No independently validated ES respondent ITQ-CA translation from this Italian study.
Other translations: IT-IT translated respondent version psychometrically evaluated in 488 Italian children/adolescents; original questionnaire is public domain per International Trauma Consortium. This study analyzed 12 symptom items only.
Target population: Children/adolescents ages 8–17 in Italy; community N432 plus residential/high-risk N56; not a clinical diagnostic validation, impairment unavailable.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Official International Trauma Consortium labels original ITQ-CA public domain/free-to-use, but Italian adapted wording/version attribution, final 21-item files and scoring/clinical safeguards must be confirmed separately. OA article CC BY does not prove every adapted component commercially reusable. No activation.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / CLINICIAN_ONLY / MINORS. 21 administered total, ONLY 12 symptom items included in psychometric models; impairment data incomplete, so NO PTSD/CPTSD diagnosis/cutoffs based on study. Italian is studied translated locale; original EN and adult ITQ keys are NOT interchangeable. Need consent/assent and qualified trauma-care safeguards.

Instrument (EN): Impact of Illness Scale — Spanish validated respondent adaptation in first-episode psychosis
Scales / measured domains (EN): Subjectively perceived adverse impact of illness on everyday life, roles and relationships; one factor, one overall impact construct
Research provenance: Martínez-Gómez S et al., The Spanish Journal of Psychology, published 2026-07-10, DOI 10.1017/SJP.2026.10035, vol29 e20. 141 people in first-episode psychosis care in Spain. Spanish translation with reverse translation of earlier English Klimidis IIS; nine-item CFA one factor CFI .998 TLI .997 RMSEA .054; Cronbach alpha .94, omega .95; test-retest moderate.
DB locales: No IIS-ES-ES-9 live Supabase published edition; research-only.
EN form: Original nine-item English IIS is the parent; 2026 study does not independently validate EN translation.
RU form: No RU respondent IIS adaptation validated by this study.
ES form: ES-ES psychometrically studied nine-item respondent edition of existing English original in Spain, n141; back-translation; single factor.
Other translations: Spanish self-report respondent edition in first-episode psychosis, N141; not a general population or EN/RU norm.
Target population: Patients with first-episode psychosis in specialist services in Spain (N141; mean age35.7), psychiatric care.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: OA article CC BY covers the publication but not automatically original Klimidis IIS item rights, translation/online commercial hosting, scoring, interpretation or clinical use. Secure permissions and supervised protocols first.
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / CLINICIAN_ONLY. 9-item single-factor symptom-impact appraisal (NOT psychosis diagnostic tool). 141 clinical participants; moderate test-retest and limited external replication. No original/Spanish items, clinical scoring, norm cutoffs, crisis workflow or SaaS activation before authorization and qualified review.
